ogTitle: 10 Most Popular Restaurants in Phrae 2026 — Eat Like a Phrae Local
ogDesc: Northern Thai food, nam yoi noodles, laab in the Nam Khong district, and wooden-house cafés in the old city — 10 restaurants Phrae locals take people to, with neighborhoods, highlights, prices, and trip tips.
eyebrow: Eat like a Phrae local · Updated 2026
intro: Phrae is a small city in a valley where the food still carries its original flavors. From khanom sen (rice noodles in pork broth) inside the old walled city to nam yoi khanom chin that you can barely find outside Mueang Pae, to Northern-style laab at well-loved spots in the Nam Khong area and wooden-house cafés in the old wiang (inner city). We've gathered 10 restaurants that Phrae locals genuinely sit down at — proper Northern-style restaurants, regular khanom chin spots, and cafés the townspeople visit every morning. Choose your direction and go.
chips: 🍜 Khanom sen and nam yoi khanom chin — Mueang Pae local specialties
🌶️ Northern-style laab in Nam Khong and Pa Maet
☕ Wooden-house cafés in the old wiang
💸 From 30 THB per dish — budget-friendly street food

blocks.html:
People often say Phrae is just a place to pass through on the way to Nan — but stop to eat and you quickly discover that the city's real appeal is local food that still holds its original flavor. Inside the old wiang walls, a few steps in any direction brings you to khanom sen shops, multi-sauce khanom chin, and wooden-house cafés converted from hundred-year-old homes. A short distance outside the walls toward Pa Maet and the Nam Khong intersection is the laab district — Northern-style laab, jin nueng, lu, and tom zaeb that locals gather for in the evenings. And the true signature of Mueang Pae is "nam yoi khanom chin" — a thick, blood-based chilli relish that is nearly impossible to find outside Phrae. Come to Phrae and make a point of trying it.

Every restaurant on this list has its own story. Hom 2493 occupies a two-storey teak house beside the old city wall, serving khanom sen pork broth and phad mi hom that have become a landmark for visitors to the wiang. Punjai offers a choice of up to seven different sauces on a single plate of khanom chin. Pa Ma Laab Nam Khong and Krua Jin Sot are the two Northern laab restaurants Phrae people nominate. For cafés, Charlotte Hut has been earning Users' Choice awards since 2010, and Slope Coffee Baan Baew is the slanting wooden-house café that has become the city's most photographed landmark. Read to the end and plan your eating trip — we've laid out the neighborhoods and the best dishes already.

blocks.name: Hom 2493
blocks.signature: Khanom sen pork broth, phad mi hom, fish sauce fried chicken wings, soft-bone pork soup
blocks.descHtml:
If you arrive in Phrae and want to eat local food in an atmosphere that genuinely feels like sitting down at a Northern Thai relative's house, Hom 2493 is the place many people recommend for a first meal. The restaurant occupies an old multi-decade teak house ("2493" is the Thai year the house was built; "hom" is a Northern dialect word meaning "gather together"). The owners converted the ground floor into a restaurant with garden seating beside the old city wall in the wiang district — easy to continue walking from here to other old-city sights. A good choice for people who want both good food and a photogenic stop in one place.

The most talked-about dish is khanom sen nam moo — essentially khanom chin in a Northern-style clear pork broth with soft-bone pork, lightly flavored and smooth. Multiple reviews agree: coming to Phrae without eating this means you haven't really arrived. The other must is phad mi hom — fragrant, pleasantly chewy noodles. Fish sauce fried chicken wings and makwen-spiced fried chicken are crispy outside, soft inside, with a clear Northern-herb fragrance. Those who like bold flavors can order tum hom (a spiced pounded salad) or tum taeng moo yor. Close with sakhu piak coconut — sweet, cold, refreshing young coconut tapioca.

Prices are very friendly: noodle dishes starting in the low tens of baht; most dishes around 50–80 THB; roughly 100–250 THB per head for a comfortable meal. The combination of great food, low prices, and a beautiful setting means the restaurant fills up nearly every day, especially at midday. Google rating is 4.6 from over 500 reviewers.

Open 09:00–16:00 daily — primarily a lunch venue, not open for dinner. During peak hours there may be a short queue as seating is not large. Arriving before midday is the comfortable approach. Parking is limited in the old-city area; for larger groups, allow a little extra time.
mustOrder: Khanom sen pork broth with soft-bone pork
Fish sauce fried chicken wings / makwen fried chicken
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Phrae, midday Northern-style food in a wooden-house atmosphere

blocks.name: Khao Soi Jae Lek Pratu Chai
blocks.area: Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District (Pratu Chai area, city ring road), Phrae
blocks.signature: Chicken khao soi / beef khao soi (house-made khao soi noodles), braised chicken leg, khao kha moo
blocks.descHtml:
Wake up in Phrae and want a warm breakfast that locals consider the city's own — this restaurant is what many people think of first. Khao Soi Jae Lek Pratu Chai is in the Pratu Chai area, Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District — selling khao soi for decades until it became a beloved institution that Phrae residents grew up tasting. What sets it apart is that the khao soi noodles are made from scratch following the restaurant's own recipe: the noodles are fresh, pleasantly chewy, and silky — completely unlike ready-made noodles elsewhere. A good introduction to Phrae for anyone who wants authentic Northern food without a long search.

The most popular orders are chicken khao soi and beef khao soi. The chicken is braised until the meat falls away from a whole drumstick; the beef is slow-simmered until tender. The broth is the real hero — multiple reviewers agree it's fragrant with curry spice, rich and full-flavored, without being heavy or greasy. Many diners say they barely need to season it at all. Each bowl arrives with crispy fried noodles on top, pickled vegetables, shallots, and a wedge of lime to adjust the flavor. Still hungry? Add khao kha moo or dim sum.

Very wallet-friendly — khao soi around 40–50 THB per bowl; other dishes similar; well under 100 THB per head. The setting is a casual, unpretentious local shop. Open from around 07:30 to 15:30 daily — works for either breakfast or lunch. Located in the Pratu Chai area, which is a great food neighborhood in the city. Easy to continue walking around the old city afterward.

The shop sells out quickly and closes in the afternoon — if you're specifically coming for the khao soi, arriving in the morning to midday is the safe play. On weekends a short queue may form. But a bowl of fresh-noodle khao soi with this kind of broth keeps both locals and visitors coming back.
blocks.bestFor: First breakfast in Phrae, khao soi and Northern food lovers

blocks.name: Punjai
blocks.area: Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District, Phrae
blocks.signature: Khanom chin with 6 sauces (nam ngiew / nam ya pa / nam phrik etc.), Punjai set, nam phrik nam yoi
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Phrae and want khanom chin that you can rarely find anywhere else, Punjai is the restaurant that Phrae residents like to recommend to others. The key draw that makes this place unlike any other is the "separate-sauce" khanom chin format — up to 7 different sauces available in a single set: Mueang Phrae nam ngiew, Chiang Mai-style nam ngiew, pla chon nam ya, nam ya pa, nam phrik, green curry, and nam phrik nam yoi. For those who love trying multiple flavors in one meal, ordering the Punjai set and working through each sauce one by one is the way to go. Excellent for families and groups.

The signature that reviewers mention most is the nam phrik nam yoi — Phrae's local specialty made from roasted chillies, shallots, and crispy fried garlic: fragrant, well-rounded, the kind of thing many people say they need to buy to take home. The Phrae-style nam ngiew is a local recipe with a flavor distinct from standard Northern-style nam ngiew elsewhere. Beyond khanom chin, there is also chicken and pork khao soi at 50 THB per bowl, beef khao soi at 70 THB, moo sa-tae, som tum, grilled chicken, and khanom pang na moo as extras.

The restaurant is spacious, decorated with wood and greenery, comfortable to sit in, with parking. Reviews note that even when busy, food comes quickly and service is good. Average price under 100 THB per person. Central location in a lane beside the Phrae Post Office, opposite Wat Phra Bat Ming Mueang — easy to find. Open daily morning to afternoon. If you're planning to make this a first or second meal in Phrae, arrive mid-morning as the restaurant closes in the afternoon and popular items like nam phrik nam yoi can sell out early.
blocks.bestFor: First or second meal of a Phrae trip, families and groups

blocks.name: Pa Ma Laab (Nam Khong)
blocks.area: Pa Maet, Mueang Phrae District, Phrae
blocks.signature: Laab jin suk, jin nueng with khaa chilli dip, lu, grilled neck pork, tom zaeb beef tendon
blocks.descHtml:
Pa Ma Laab (Nam Khong) is one of Phrae's most established laab restaurants, talked about for several generations by people who grew up here. If you want Northern Thai local food in its original form — not sweetened for tourists — this is the restaurant to visit. The setting is a large corrugated-roof wooden building with plenty of tables, a relaxed home-style atmosphere, and customers who eat in or stop to take food away. Reviewers across multiple platforms consistently describe the flavors as "genuinely local" — bold in the way Northern laab is meant to be.

The most regularly ordered dishes are laab jin suk and lu — the restaurant's main event. The spice mix is fragrant, the laab chilli (phrik laab) flavor comes through clearly. Another strong recommendation is jin nueng jum nam phrik khaa (steamed meat with galangal chilli dip) — soft, paired with a deeply flavored dip. Grilled neck pork is a popular side, aromatic from the grill without being dry. For those who like a hot broth, tom zaeb beef tendon is rich and smooth. Also on the menu: pork laab kuaw, grilled milk-bread, various yam salads, gaeng om, and chilli-fermented-fish papaya salad — a full rice-sharing spread.

Prices are approachable; most dishes in the 101–250 THB per person range. Good value for groups sharing. Located in the Pa Maet / Nam Khong area at the entrance road to Ban Song Khwae, left side before entering Phrae city. Convenient parking. Open daily around 09:00–21:00 (occasionally closed on Buddhist holy days) — works for both lunch and dinner.

This restaurant remains popular because it is a long-standing restaurant that has kept its flavor. Many Phrae residents name it as one of the laab places to try at least once. Worth noting: the flavor runs spicy and bold in authentic Northern laab style. Those who don't eat spicy should mention this to the staff. Lu is a raw dish — those who are not comfortable with that can order laab jin suk or jin nueng instead.
mustOrder: Jin nueng with galangal chilli dip
blocks.bestFor: Authentic local meal in Phrae, group dining
blocks.spice: Boldly spicy — classic Northern laab style

blocks.name: Krua Jin Sot Local Food
blocks.signature: Hok nueng, yam sai wan, laab khom suk, gaeng om beef, lu moo, tom khom
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Phrae and want genuinely local Northern Thai food — the kind locals actually eat, not a version adjusted for visitors — Krua Jin Sot is where the townspeople tend to go. The restaurant is near Pa Maet, at the Nam Khong intersection on the Phrae–Long Road, and has been open for over twenty years, becoming the go-to for anyone craving laab, lu, and bold local dishes. The name "Jin Sot" means "fresh meat," which is exactly what the place is built around. Works well for groups and families who enjoy sharing and eating meat.

The dishes that earn the most repeat orders are the various laab khom (bitter laab) — both raw and cooked — with reviewers on food platforms praising fine-minced tender meat, a bitterness that's pleasant without being harsh. Lu moo with deep, full-flavored intensity, grilled neck pork that's fragrant, yam sai wan (offal salad), gaeng om beef with rounded flavor, hok nueng, and tom khom (bitter soup) drunk hot with fresh vegetables and sticky rice. Those who love bold Northern flavors will feel at home; anyone unfamiliar with bitter or raw ingredients can ask the restaurant and choose the suk (cooked) options first.

The setting is an everyday local-restaurant atmosphere — lots of tables, comfortable, no need to dress up. Has parking. Suitable for midday through dinner without formality. Per-head price in the low hundreds of THB; sharing many dishes in a group keeps it great value. Google Maps rating around 4.3 from hundreds of reviews, reflecting consistent appreciation from both Phrae locals and passing visitors.

Open daily from around 09:30 to 20:00. At lunch and dinner on weekends the restaurant fills up; large groups should allow a little extra time. Some dishes are genuine local specialties — raw laab or tom khom. If you're unfamiliar, ordering small amounts to taste first and then adding more of what works is the relaxed approach.
blocks.bestFor: Group dining, meat lovers, genuinely bold Northern flavors
blocks.spice: Spicy and bold (laab / lu / tom khom are punchy)

blocks.name: Khanom Sen Nam Yoi Mueang Pae Kad Nam Thong (Jo Yok)
blocks.signature: Khanom chin nam yoi (nam phrik nam yoi / pork blood broth), khao kan jin, tam kaep moo
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Phrae wanting a genuinely local specialty, Khanom Sen Nam Yoi Mueang Pae Kad Nam Thong — known to regulars as "Jo Yok" — is the spot to mark on your map. The restaurant's signature is fresh house-made khanom chin noodles: thin, soft, fragrant, served in a clear pork bone broth with a touch of pork blood. Once the noodles arrive, you walk to the central boat in the middle of the restaurant and ladle on as much nam phrik nam yoi and blanched vegetables as you like — unlimited. Perfect for anyone who wants genuine Phrae local flavors and anyone on a budget looking for a filling meal for a few dozen baht.

The must-order is khanom chin nam yoi — topped with nam phrik nam yoi, which resembles a pork-fat relish mixed with crispy fried garlic. The flavor is gently salty-sweet with good heat, and many people say they eat through it so happily the saliva flows as the name suggests. Another dish Phrae locals like to order alongside is khao kan jin, and tam kaep moo (papaya salad with crispy pork rind pounded in). Those who like it spicy can try tum pa or salted-egg tum. Reviews consistently praise the genuinely fresh noodles, the punchy nam phrik, and excellent value for money.

Prices are gentle: khanom chin from about 30–40 THB per dish; tam kaep moo around 60 THB; well under 100 THB per head. The atmosphere is a casual local restaurant with plenty of seating, easy roadside parking. Located on Nam Thong Bypass Road in the Na Jak area. Open daily mid-morning to afternoon, around 10:30–16:30. For a midday meal, arriving before 13:00 means the full range is still available.

This restaurant is well known because it received a provincial specialty award from the Phrae Chamber of Commerce and is one of the most talked-about nam yoi khanom chin restaurants among both tourists and locals. The chilli heat in the nam phrik is moderate and easy to control at the self-serve station. Those who don't eat spicy can ladle on just a little and pile on more blanched vegetables.
mustOrder: Khanom chin nam yoi (nam phrik nam yoi / pork blood broth)
blocks.bestFor: Midday local specialty on a budget
blocks.spice: Medium (adjust yourself at the self-serve station)

blocks.name: Rom Mai Yai Restaurant
blocks.signature: Fried pla kaphong with fish sauce reduction, crispy German pork knuckle, Rom Mai Yai yam salad, hot-plate grilled neck pork
blocks.descHtml:
Rom Mai Yai Restaurant is one of Phrae's large gathering restaurants that locals book for family meals. Located in the Pa Maet area on Phaya Phon Road, the venue has multiple seating zones: inside the main building, open-air tables under large trees beside a pond, and private karaoke rooms. Good for large groups who want a single venue that covers Thai, Northern Thai, and seafood across the table, with live music some evenings that keeps the mood easy and informal.

The most frequently ordered dishes are fried pla kaphong with fish sauce reduction — a large fish, firm flesh, skin crisped up, then finished with a sweet-salty sauce — and the signature crispy German pork knuckle: crackling skin, soft meat, served with a spicy dipping sauce. Hot-plate grilled neck pork arrives sizzling and juicy; Rom Mai Yai yam salad (the house specialty) delivers a punchy sour-spicy hit that opens the appetite. Those who prefer tom yam can try the coconut young tom yam with river prawn in a rich broth. Reviews consistently describe well-rounded flavors, clean execution, fast service, and a restaurant that earns its long-standing reputation.

Overall Google rating around 4.2 from over a thousand reviewers — a restaurant that has held its position as one of Phrae's famous spots. Highlights frequently mentioned: spacious grounds, easy parking, good service, and prices that make sense relative to the setting. Price range roughly 251–500 THB per person. The menu has English descriptions — international visitors can order without difficulty.

Open daily around 11:00–22:00. On holiday evenings crowds build; for large groups or if you want a nice waterside spot, calling ahead to reserve is the comfortable approach. If you come to Phrae wanting one big comfortable meal where the whole group can order freely, this restaurant delivers.
mustOrder: Fried pla kaphong with fish sauce reduction
blocks.bestFor: Dinner with family or a large group, riverside atmosphere with live music

blocks.name: Charlotte Hut Coffee & Tea Bar
blocks.area: Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District (Soi Mueang Hit, old-city area), Phrae
blocks.signature: Charlotte Hut Signature, Okura Matcha, maprang cold brew, bakery
blocks.descHtml:
Walking through the Phrae old-city area near Soi Mueang Hit and looking for a quiet spot to sit with a coffee — Charlotte Hut Coffee & Tea Bar is the name Phrae people think of first. The café has been open long enough to become the city's best-loved coffee stop, set in a cosy wooden house surrounded by greenery with a koi pond and photo spots both inside and out. Perfect for solo visitors, a date, or a long catch-up with friends.

The most popular orders are the Charlotte Hut Signature house coffee, Okura Matcha (enjoyed especially as an iced oat-milk matcha latte), and maprang cold brew — a local fruit cold-brew combination that is refreshingly tart-sweet. Those with a sweet tooth should try the homemade cakes: reviewers say they're attractive enough to photograph and taste genuinely good with multiple options available. The café also serves Twinings tea in a pot.

For flavor, most reviews give it a pass — smooth, aromatic coffee, staff who know their beans and serve with a friendly manner. Drinks around 45–70 THB — mid-range by Phrae standards. A few reviewers note the price is slightly on the high side for the town, but the atmosphere and quality balance it out. On weekends and festivals the café fills and tables take a little longer to find; coming in the morning avoids the rush.

Located at 8/1 Mueang Hit Road, Nai Wiang sub-district, Mueang Phrae. Open daily 08:00–17:30. Parking available. The old-city location means you can walk on to other sights afterward, plus the garden setting and cakes photograph well — reasons Charlotte Hut keeps drawing both locals and visitors.
blocks.bestFor: Café chill with friends or a partner in the old city

blocks.name: Slope Coffee Baan Baew
blocks.area: Nai Wiang, Mueang Phrae District, Phrae
blocks.signature: Drip coffee / specialty coffee, Nong Fai drink (kiwi-apple-lemon soda)
blocks.descHtml:
Walking through the Phrae old-city area near the walking street and spotting a charmingly crooked, slightly slanted old wooden house — that is Slope Coffee Baan Baew, a legendary café of Phrae. "Baew" comes from a Northern dialect word meaning crooked or askew, because this hundred-year-old wooden house has floors that tilt, a sloping roof, and pillars that have warped with time. The owners turned that crookedness into the café's charm. A great fit for people who love vintage wooden-house cafés, photography, and a slow-paced coffee in the old city.

Coffee enthusiasts should not miss the house drip coffee and specialty coffee. Multiple reviews say the coffee here is deep and aromatic, the espresso shots have dimension and smoothness — good for those who like their coffee bold. For non-coffee drinkers there is "Nong Fai" — a signature drink of kiwi-apple-lemon soda that is refreshingly tart-sweet. Other options: iced latte, mocha, cappuccino, cold brew, and homemade cakes — the coconut cake gets particular praise from reviewers. A charming detail: order a coffee and a biscuit shaped like a letter comes with it.

The atmosphere is the star. Inside: vintage television sets, old-model fans, wooden furniture, and collected objects that invite reflection. Behind the café is a small garden under large trees — comfortable, breezy, easy to sit for a long time. Prices are friendly: most drinks around 55–75 THB. Located in the wiang, opposite Wat Phong Sunan, near Kad Kong Kao and the walking street. Open daily 09:00–17:30.

This café endures because it combines everything visitors to Phrae tend to look for: good coffee, a hundred-year-old wooden house with a story, photo-worthy corners in every direction, and prices that are easy to say yes to. Google review score 4.6 from hundreds of reviewers. On weekends crowds build and quiet corners may take a little patience; parking is limited in the old-city area. Allow a small buffer for the walk in.
blocks.bestFor: Café lovers who enjoy vintage wooden houses and photo spots in the old city

blocks.name: Kim's Cafe'
blocks.signature: Fried red tilapia with herbs, salmon head tom yam, fusion dishes
blocks.descHtml:
Ask Phrae locals where to go for a long relaxed dinner with friends and "Kim's Cafe'" — or Kim Café as regulars call it — often comes up first. Located near Na Jak, Mueang Phrae District, opposite Mark Four department store, this semi-café semi-restaurant has been open long enough to become the city's regular meeting spot. Works well for a pair, a group, or a family — air-conditioned, easy parking, and a menu wide enough that no one needs to overthink the order.

Dishes that come up most in reviews are fried red tilapia with herbs (the fish is fluffy and crispy, scattered with fried herbs) and salmon head tom yam drunk hot. Also highly praised in reviews is the salt-fried chicken (around 90 THB per dish) — crispy skin, pleasantly salty — alongside tom zaeb pork and salt-fried garoupa (around 180 THB). The fusion element is a genuine draw: the menu mixes Thai, Chinese, Japanese, and Western dishes. Want sashimi, a salmon-nam pla ra yam, or salmon rice? It's here. Ordering across the whole table is part of the fun.

For quality, most reviews say the food is good and the portions are generous. A few note the prices run slightly higher than other Phrae restaurants, but seeing the portion sizes tends to quiet any complaint. Daytime atmosphere is bright and good for sitting down with coffee; evenings shift to a softer-lit, light-pub tone and some nights feature live music — easy to sit and talk all evening. Per-head price around 101–250 THB — comfortable for a filling meal.

Open daily 10:00–22:00. On festivals and public holidays the restaurant fills up and food can take a bit longer; large groups are advised to call ahead and book a table. Overall, a restaurant that Phrae people endorse as one that won't disappoint — varied menu, good atmosphere, open until late.
blocks.bestFor: Long evening dinner with friends or family

blocks.title: Good to Know Before Eating in Phrae

items.title: Getting around the city
items.text: The old wiang is small and easy to walk — khanom sen, khanom chin, and cafés are all within walking distance of each other. Grab in Phrae has few cars, though. If you're going to Pa Maet–Nam Khong or Kad Nam Thong, renting a motorbike or car is far more practical.

items.title: Carry cash
items.text: Local food restaurants, street vendors, and khanom chin spots mostly accept cash as the primary method. Some have PromptPay but not all. Keep small notes on you — especially for market spots like Kad Nam Thong.

items.title: Local specialties sell out early
items.text: Khanom sen pork broth, nam yoi khanom chin, and khao soi are morning-to-afternoon items. Go late and the popular ones may be sold out. For laab and sit-down Northern food restaurants, evenings work well. Beat the café rush by going before 11:00 or in the late afternoon.

items.title: Tell them your heat level
items.text: Northern food like laab, jin nueng with galangal chilli dip, and nam ngiew is genuinely bold and spicy. If you can't handle heat, let the restaurant know and they'll reduce the chilli. Nam yoi and nam ngiew have an individual spice and richness — taste before adding more seasoning.

items.title: Most menus are in Thai
items.text: Local restaurants in Phrae mostly have Thai and Northern dialect menus. English menus are available at some cafés. If unsure, point at a photo or ask for the popular dish by name — khanom sen, laab, lu — locals are friendly and happy to help.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Local food restaurants and street food in Phrae have no tipping custom — just pay the listed price. At large sit-down restaurants like Rom Mai Yai or a café, if the service impressed you, leaving a small amount is a kind gesture but never required.

blocks.title: Planning a One-Day Eating Trip in Phrae
blocks.html:
With a single day, start in the morning inside the old wiang. Walk in to Hom 2493 for khanom sen and phad mi hom (closes at 16:00 — go late and you may miss out). Follow with multi-sauce khanom chin at Punjai, or fresh-made khao soi at Jae Lek Pratu Chai. All of these are within walking distance of each other inside the wiang.

In the afternoon, stop at a café: Charlotte Hut stands out for matcha and freshly baked goods; Slope Coffee Baan Baew is the drip-coffee-and-wooden-house spot. By evening, move out toward Pa Maet–Nam Khong and order laab jin suk, jin nueng, and tom zaeb at Pa Ma Laab or Krua Jin Sot. If you've come with a group who wants a long relaxed dinner, Rom Mai Yai on Phaya Phon Road has fried pla kaphong and German pork knuckle for sharing.

blocks.text: After a full day of eating in Phrae, staying in the old-city area means you can walk out to morning khanom sen. We've put together a selection of well-located accommodation in Phrae near the wiang — easy access to all the food spots.

faq.q: Which restaurant in Phrae is the most famous?
faq.a: For local food, Hom 2493 in the old wiang is the most talked-about restaurant among visitors to Phrae — with khanom sen pork broth and phad mi hom in an old teak house beside the city wall. For cafés, Charlotte Hut and Slope Coffee Baan Baew are the two most visited and photographed spots in the wiang.

The real Mueang Pae signature is nam yoi khanom chin — a thick chilli relish with pork blood that is nearly impossible to find outside Phrae. Try it at Khanom Sen Nam Yoi Mueang Pae Kad Nam Thong (Jo Yok). Other local staples are khanom sen pork broth, Northern-style laab, jin nueng with galangal chilli dip, and lu — all available at Pa Maet–Nam Khong restaurants.

faq.q: How much does eating in Phrae cost?
faq.a: Street food and local restaurants are very affordable. Nam yoi khanom chin starts at 30–70 THB per dish; Jae Lek khao soi is 40–50 THB per bowl. Sit-down Northern food restaurants like Pa Ma Laab or Krua Jin Sot run around 100–250 THB per person. Café drinks are 45–75 THB per glass. Rom Mai Yai, as a larger dinner restaurant, is around 251–500 THB per person.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table in advance?
faq.a: Most local food restaurants and cafés in Phrae are walk-in. On long weekends, popular cafés like Slope Coffee Baan Baew and Charlotte Hut fill up and tables take longer to find. For large groups or Rom Mai Yai on a Saturday evening, calling ahead to reserve a table is the comfortable approach.

faq.q: Which restaurants are open in the evening or late?
faq.a: Northern food restaurants in the Pa Maet–Nam Khong area like Pa Ma Laab and Krua Jin Sot are good evening spots with extended hours. Rom Mai Yai on Phaya Phon Road closes around 22:00. Morning local food like Hom 2493, nam yoi khanom chin, and Jae Lek khao soi run morning-to-afternoon — go late and they may be sold out.
